paragraphs.sourceText: Your social life is defined as “the activities you do with other people, for pleasure, when you are not working.” It’s important to have a social life, but what’s right for one person won’t be right for another. Some of us feel energised by spending lots of time with others, 1 some of us may feel drained, even if it’s doing something we enjoy.
paragraphs.translationZh: 您的社交生活被定义为“当您不工作时，为了娱乐而与其他人一起进行的活动”。拥有社交生活很重要，但适合一个人的东西不一定适合另一个人。我们中的一些人因为花大量时间与他人在一起而感到精力充沛，而另一些人可能会感到精疲力竭，即使是在做我们喜欢的事情。

paragraphs.sourceText: This is why finding a 2 in your social life is key. Spending too much time on your own, not 3 others, can make you feel lonely and 4 . Loneliness is known to impact on your mental health and 5 a low mood. Anyone can feel lonely at any time. This might be especially true if, 6 , you are working from home and you are 7 on the usual social conversations that happen in an office. Other life changes can 8 periods of loneliness too, such as retirement, changing jobs or becoming a parent.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这就是为什么在社交生活中找到平衡是关键。花太多时间独处，不与他人见面，会让你感到孤独和孤立。众所周知，孤独会影响您的心理健康并导致情绪低落。任何人都可能在任何时候感到孤独。例如，如果您在家工作并且错过了在办公室进行的常见社交对话，则尤其如此。其他生活变化也可能引发孤独期，例如退休、换工作或成为父母。

paragraphs.sourceText: It’s important to recognise these feelings of loneliness. There are ways to 9 a social life, but it can feel overwhelming 10 . It’s a great idea to start by thinking about hobbies you enjoy. You can then find groups and activities related to those where you will be able to meet 11 people. There are groups aimed at new parents, at those who want to 12 a new sport for the first time, or networking events for those in the same profession to meet up and 13 ideas.
paragraphs.translationZh: 认识到这些孤独感很重要。有很多方法可以恢复社交生活，但一开始可能会让人感到不知所措。从考虑你喜欢的爱好开始是个好主意。然后，您可以找到与您能够结识志同道合的人相关的团体和活动。有些团体是针对新父母、想要第一次尝试新运动的人，或者是为同一行业的人士提供聚会和分享想法的社交活动。

paragraphs.sourceText: On the other hand, it’s 14 possible to have too much of a social life. If you feel like you’re always doing something and there is never any 15 in your calendar for downtime, you could suffer social burnout or social 16 . We all have our own social limit and it’s important to recognise when you’re feeling like it’s all too much. Low mood, low energy, irritability and trouble sleeping could all be 17 of poor social health. Make sure you 18 some time in your diary when you’re 19 for socialising and use this time to relax, 20 and recover.
paragraphs.translationZh: 另一方面，也可能有太多的社交生活。如果您觉得自己总是在做某事，并且日历中没有任何休息时间，那么您可能会遭受社交倦怠或社交疲劳。我们都有自己的社交限制，当您感觉自己的社交限制太多时，认识到这一点很重要。情绪低落、精力不足、烦躁和睡眠困难都可能是社交健康状况不佳的迹象。确保在日记中标记出您无法参加社交活动的时间，并利用这段时间放松、休息和恢复。

paragraphs.sourceText: Read the following four texts. Answer the questions below each text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (40 points)
paragraphs.translationZh: 阅读下面四篇课文。选择 A、B、C 或 D 来回答每篇文章下方的问题。在答题卡上标记您的答案。 （40分）

paragraphs.sourceText: In her new book Cogs and Monsters: What Economics Is, and What It Should Be, Diane Coyle, an economist at Cambridge University, argues that the digital economy requires new ways of thinking about progress. “Whatever we mean by the economy growing, by things getting better, the gains will have to be more evenly shared than in the recent past,” she writes. “An economy of tech millionaires or billionaires and gig workers, with middle-income jobs undercut by automation, will not be politically sustainable.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 剑桥大学经济学家黛安·科伊尔在她的新书《齿轮与怪物：经济学是什么，以及它应该是什么》中指出，数字经济需要新的思维方式来思考进步。她写道：“无论我们所说的经济增长、情况好转是什么意思，收益的分享都必须比最近更均匀。” “科技百万富翁或亿万富翁和零工工人的经济，以及中等收入工作岗位因自动化而受到削弱，在政治上是不可持续的。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Improving living standards and increasing prosperity for more people will require greater use of digital technologies to boost productivity in various sectors, including health care and construction, says Coyle. But people can’t be expected to embrace the changes if they’re not seeing the benefits — if they’re just seeing good jobs being destroyed.
paragraphs.translationZh: 科伊尔表示，要提高更多人的生活水平并促进繁荣，就需要更多地利用数字技术来提高各个行业的生产力，包括医疗保健和建筑业。但如果人们没有看到好处——如果他们只是看到好工作被摧毁，就不能指望他们接受这些变化。

paragraphs.sourceText: In a recent interview, Coyle said she fears that tech’s inequality problem could be a roadblock to deploying AI. “We’re talking about disruption,” she says. “These are transformative technologies that change the ways we spend our time every day, that change business models that succeed.” To make such “tremendous changes,” she adds, you need social buy-in.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在最近的一次采访中，科伊尔表示，她担心科技领域的不平等问题可能会成为部署人工智能的障碍。 “我们正在谈论颠覆，”她说。 “这些都是变革性的技术，它们改变了我们每天度过时间的方式，改变了成功的商业模式。”她补充道，要做出如此“巨大的改变”，你需要社会的支持。

paragraphs.sourceText: Instead, says Coyle, resentment is simmering among many as the benefits are perceived to go to elites in a handful of prosperous cities.
paragraphs.translationZh: 科伊尔表示，相反，许多人的不满情绪正在酝酿之中，因为人们认为这些好处惠及了少数繁荣城市的精英。

paragraphs.sourceText: According to the Brookings Institution, a short list of eight American cities that included San Francisco, San Jose, Boston, and Seattle had roughly 38% of all tech jobs by 2019. New AI technologies are particularly concentrated: Brookings’s Mark Muro and Sifan Liu estimate that just 15 cities account for two-thirds of the AI assets and capabilities in the United States.
paragraphs.translationZh: 根据布鲁金斯学会的数据，到 2019 年，旧金山、圣何塞、波士顿和西雅图等 8 个美国城市占据了所有科技岗位的约 38%。新的人工智能技术尤其集中：布鲁金斯学会的 Mark Muro 和 Sifan Liu 估计，仅 15 个城市就拥有美国人工智能资产和能力的三分之二。

paragraphs.sourceText: The dominance of a few cities in the invention and commercialization of AI means that geographical disparities in wealth will continue to soar. Not only will this foster political and social unrest, but it could, as Coyle suggests, hold back the sorts of AI technologies needed for regional economies to grow.
paragraphs.translationZh: 少数城市在人工智能发明和商业化方面占据主导地位，这意味着财富的地域差距将继续扩大。这不仅会加剧政治和社会动荡，而且正如科伊尔所说，它可能会阻碍区域经济增长所需的人工智能技术。

paragraphs.sourceText: Part of the solution could lie in somehow loosening the stranglehold that Big Tech has on defining the AI agenda. That will likely take increased federal funding for research independent of the tech giants.
paragraphs.translationZh: 部分解决方案可能在于以某种方式放松大型科技公司对定义人工智能议程的束缚。这可能需要增加联邦资金用于独立于科技巨头的研究。

paragraphs.sourceText: A more immediate response is to broaden our digital imaginations to conceive of AI technologies that don’t simply replace jobs but expand opportunities in the sectors that different parts of the country care most about, like health care, education, and manufacturing.
paragraphs.translationZh: 更直接的反应是扩大我们的数字想象力，构想人工智能技术，这些技术不仅会取代工作岗位，而且会扩大该国不同地区最关心的行业的机会，例如医疗保健、教育和制造业。

paragraphs.sourceText: The UK is facing a future construction crisis because of a failure to plant trees to produce wood, Confor has warned. The forestry and wood trade body has called for urgent action to reduce the country’s reliance on timber imports and provide a stable supply of wood for future generations. Currently only 20 percent of the UK’s wood requirement is home-grown while it remains the second-largest net importer of timber in the world.
paragraphs.translationZh: Confor警告说，由于无法种植树木来生产木材，英国未来将面临建筑危机。林业和木材贸易机构呼吁采取紧急行动，减少该国对木材进口的依赖，并为子孙后代提供稳定的木材供应。目前，英国只有 20% 的木材需求是本土生产的，但英国仍然是世界第二大木材净进口国。

paragraphs.sourceText: Coming at a time of fresh incentives from the UK government for landowners to grow more trees, the trade body says these don’t go far enough and fail to promote the benefits of planting them to boost timber supplies. “Not only are we facing a carbon crisis now, but we will also be facing a future construction crisis because of a failure to plant trees to produce wood,” said Stuart Goodall, chief executive of Confor. “For decades we have not taken responsibility for investing in our domestic wood supply, leaving us exposed to fluctuating prices and fighting for future supplies of wood as global demand rises and our own supplies fall.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 该贸易机构表示，在英国政府出台新的激励措施鼓励土地所有者种植更多树木之际，这些措施还不够，也未能宣传种植树木以增加木材供应的好处。 Confor 首席执行官斯图尔特·古道尔 (Stuart Goodall) 表示：“我们现在不仅面临碳危机，未来还将面临建筑危机，因为无法种植树木来生产木材。” “几十年来，我们没有承担起投资国内木材供应的责任，这使我们面临价格波动的风险，并随着全球需求的上升和我们自己的供应下降而争夺未来的木材供应。”

paragraphs.sourceText: The UK has ideal conditions for growing wood to build low-carbon homes and is a global leader in certifying that its forests are sustainably managed, Confor says. While around three quarters of Scottish homes are built from Scottish timber, the use of home-grown wood in England is only around 25 percent. The causes of the UK’s current position are complex and range from outdated perceptions of productive forestry to the decimation of trees by grey squirrels. It also encompasses significant hesitation on behalf of farmers and other landowners to invest in long-term planting projects.
paragraphs.translationZh: Confor表示，英国拥有种植木材建造低碳住宅的理想条件，并且在证明其森林得到可持续管理方面处于全球领先地位。虽然大约四分之三的苏格兰房屋是用苏格兰木材建造的，但英格兰本土木材的使用率只有 25% 左右。英国目前处境的原因很复杂，从对生产性林业的过时观念到灰松鼠对树木的大量砍伐。它还包括农民和其他土地所有者对投资长期种植项目的严重犹豫。

paragraphs.sourceText: While productive tree planting can deliver real financial benefits to rural economies and contribute to the UK’s net-zero strategy, the focus of government support continues to be on food production and the rewilding and planting of native woodland solely for biodiversity. Goodall added: “While food production and biodiversity health are clearly of critical importance, we need our land to also provide secure supplies of wood for construction, manufacturing and contribute to net-zero.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 虽然生产性植树可以为农村经济带来真正的经济利益，并有助于英国的净零排放战略，但政府支持的重点仍然是粮食生产以及纯粹为了生物多样性而重新野化和种植原生林地。古道尔补充道：“虽然粮食生产和生物多样性健康显然至关重要，但我们还需要我们的土地为建筑、制造业提供安全的木材供应，并为净零排放做出贡献。”

paragraphs.sourceText: “While the UK government has stated its ambition for more tree planting, there has been little action on the ground. Confor is now calling for much greater impetus behind those aspirations to ensure we have enough wood to meet increasing demand.”
paragraphs.translationZh: “虽然英国政府已经表达了更多植树的雄心，但实际行动却很少。Confor 现在呼吁为这些愿望提供更大的推动力，以确保我们有足够的木材来满足不断增长的需求。”

paragraphs.sourceText: One of the biggest challenges in keeping unsafe aging drivers off the road is convincing them that it’s time to turn over the keys. “It’s a complete life-changer” when someone stops — or is forced to stop — driving, said former risk manager Anne M. Menke.
paragraphs.translationZh: 让不安全的老年司机远离道路的最大挑战之一是说服他们是时候交出钥匙了。前风险经理 Anne M. Menke 表示，当有人停止或被迫停止驾驶时，“这将彻底改变生活”。

paragraphs.sourceText: “The American Medical Association advises physicians that in situations where clear evidence of substantial driving impairment implies a strong threat to patient and public safety, and where the physician’s advice to discontinue driving privileges is ignored, it is desirable and ethical to notify the Department of Motor Vehicles,” Menke wrote. “Some states require physicians to report, others allow but do not mandate reports, while a few consider a report a breach of confidentiality. There could be liability and penalties if a physician does not act in accordance with state laws on reporting and confidentiality,” she counseled.
paragraphs.translationZh: 门克写道：“美国医学会建议医生，如果明显证据表明严重驾驶障碍意味着对患者和公共安全构成严重威胁，并且医生停止驾驶特权的建议被忽视，则最好通知机动车辆部，这也是合乎道德的。” “一些州要求医生报告，另一些州允许但不强制报告，而少数州则认为报告违反保密性。如果医生不按照州有关报告和保密的法律行事，可能会承担责任和处罚，”她建议道。

paragraphs.sourceText: Part of the problem in keeping older drivers safe is that the difficulties are addressed piecemeal by different professions with different focuses, including gerontologists, highway administration officials, automotive engineers and others, said gerontologist Elizabeth Dugan. “There’s not a National Institute of Older Driver Studies,” she said. “We need better evidence on what makes drivers unsafe” and what can help, said Dugan.
paragraphs.translationZh: 老年学家伊丽莎白·杜根 (Elizabeth Dugan) 表示，保障老年驾驶员安全的部分问题在于，不同专业人士以不同的侧重点零碎地解决了这些困难，其中包括老年学家、高速公路管理官员、汽车工程师等。 “没有国家老年驾驶员研究所，”她说。杜根说，“我们需要更好的证据来证明是什么导致司机不安全”以及什么可以提供帮助。

paragraphs.sourceText: One thing that does seem to work is requiring drivers to report in person for license renewal. Mandatory in-person renewal was associated with a 31 percent reduction in fatal crashes involving drivers 85 or older, according to one study. Passing vision tests also produced a similar decline in fatal crashes for those drivers, although there appeared to be no benefit from combining the two.
paragraphs.translationZh: 似乎确实有效的一件事是要求司机亲自报告以更新驾照。一项研究表明，强制当面续保可以使 85 岁或以上驾驶员的致命车祸减少 31%。通过视力测试也使这些司机的致命车祸发生率类似地下降，尽管将两者结合起来似乎没有任何好处。

paragraphs.sourceText: Many older drivers don’t see eye doctors or can’t afford to. Primary care providers have their hands full and may not be able to follow through with patients who have trouble driving because they can’t turn their heads or remember where they are going — or have gotten shorter and haven’t changed their seat settings sufficiently to reach car pedals easily.
paragraphs.translationZh: 许多老年司机不去看眼科医生，或者负担不起。初级保健提供者忙得不可开交，可能无法跟进那些驾驶困难的患者，因为他们无法转动头部或记住自己要去哪里，或者变得更矮并且没有充分改变座椅设置以轻松到达汽车踏板。

paragraphs.sourceText: As long as there are other cars on the roads, self-driving cars won’t solve the problems of crashes, said Dugan. Avoiding dangers posed by all those human drivers would require too many algorithms, she said. But we need to do more to improve safety, said Dugan. “If we’re going to have 100-year lives, we need cars that a 90-year-old can drive comfortably.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 杜根说，只要道路上还有其他汽车，自动驾驶汽车就无法解决碰撞问题。她说，避免所有人类司机造成的危险需要太多的算法。但杜根说，我们需要采取更多措施来提高安全性。 “如果我们想要活到 100 岁，我们就需要 90 岁的老人也能舒适地驾驶的汽车。”

paragraphs.sourceText: If you look at the apps on your phone, chances are you have at least one related to your health — and probably several. Whether it is a mental health app, a fitness tracker, a connected health device or something else, many of us are taking advantage of this technology to keep better track of our health in some shape or form. Recent research from the Organization for the Review of Care and Health Applications found that 350,000 health apps were available on the market, 90,000 of which launched in 2020 alone.
paragraphs.translationZh: 如果您查看手机上的应用程序，您可能至少有一个与您的健康相关的应用程序 - 甚至可能有多个。无论是心理健康应用程序、健身追踪器、联网健康设备还是其他产品，我们中的许多人都在利用这项技术以某种形式更好地跟踪我们的健康状况。护理和健康应用审查组织最近的研究发现，市场上有 350,000 个健康应用程序，其中 90,000 个是在 2020 年推出的。

paragraphs.sourceText: While these apps have a great deal to offer, it is not always clear how the personal information we input is collected, safeguarded and shared online. Existing health privacy law, such as the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act, is primarily focused on the way hospitals, doctors’ offices, clinics and insurance companies store health records online. The health information these apps and health data tracking wearables are collecting typically do not receive the same legal protections.
paragraphs.translationZh: 虽然这些应用程序可以提供很多功能，但我们并不总是清楚如何收集、保护和在线共享我们输入的个人信息。现有的健康隐私法，例如《健康保险流通和责任法案》，主要关注医院、医生办公室、诊所和保险公司在线存储健康记录的方式。这些应用程序和跟踪可穿戴设备收集的健康信息通常不会受到相同的法律保护。

paragraphs.sourceText: Without additional protections in place, companies may share (and potentially monetize) personal health information in a way consumers may not have authorized or anticipated. In 2021, Flo Health faced a Federal Trade Commission (FTC) investigation. The FTC alleged in a complaint that “despite express privacy claims, the company took control of users’ sensitive fertility data and shared it with third parties.” Flo Health and the FTC settled the matter with a Consent Order requiring the company to get app users’ express affirmative consent before sharing their health information as well as to instruct the third parties to delete the data they had obtained.
paragraphs.translationZh: 如果没有额外的保护措施，公司可能会以消费者未授权或预期的方式共享（并可能将其货币化）个人健康信息。 2021 年，Flo Health 面临联邦贸易委员会 (FTC) 调查。美国联邦贸易委员会在一份投诉中称，“尽管有明确的隐私声明，该公司还是控制了用户的敏感生育数据，并将其与第三方共享。” Flo Health 和联邦贸易委员会通过一项同意令解决了此事，要求该公司在分享用户的健康信息之前获得应用程序用户的明确同意，并指示第三方删除他们获得的数据。

paragraphs.sourceText: Section 5 of the FTC Act empowers the FTC to initiate enforcement action against unfair or deceptive acts, meaning the FTC can only act after the fact if a company’s privacy practices are misleading or cause unjustified consumer harm. While the FTC is doing what it can to ensure apps are keeping their promises to consumers around the handling of their sensitive health information, the rate at which these health apps are hitting the market demonstrates just how immense of a challenge this is.
paragraphs.translationZh: 《联邦贸易委员会法案》第 5 条授权联邦贸易委员会针对不公平或欺骗行为发起执法行动，这意味着联邦贸易委员会只能在公司的隐私做法具有误导性或造成不合理的消费者伤害的情况下采取事后行动。虽然联邦贸易委员会正在尽其所能确保应用程序在处理敏感健康信息方面履行对消费者的承诺，但这些健康应用程序进入市场的速度表明这是一个多么巨大的挑战。

paragraphs.sourceText: As to the prospects for federal legislation, commentators suggest that comprehensive federal privacy legislation seems unlikely in the short term. States have begun implementing their own solutions to shore up protections for consumer-generated health data. California has been at the forefront of state privacy efforts with the California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018. Virginia, Colorado and Utah have also recently passed state consumer data privacy legislation.
paragraphs.translationZh: 至于联邦立法的前景，评论人士表示，短期内似乎不太可能出台全面的联邦隐私立法。各州已开始实施自己的解决方案，以加强对消费者生成的健康数据的保护。通过《2018 年加州消费者隐私法案》，加州一直走在州隐私保护工作的最前沿。弗吉尼亚州、科罗拉多州和犹他州最近也通过了州消费者数据隐私立法。

paragraphs.translationZh: 阅读以下文本，并将左栏中的每个编号项目与右栏中的相应信息相匹配。右栏中有两个额外的选项。在答题卡上标记您的答案。 （10分）

paragraphs.sourceText: How Colleges Weigh Applicants’ Extracurricular Activities
paragraphs.translationZh: 大学如何衡量申请人的课外活动

paragraphs.sourceText: High school students eager to stand out in the college application process often participate in a litany of extracurricular activities hoping to bolster their chances of admission to a selective undergraduate institution.
paragraphs.translationZh: 渴望在大学申请过程中脱颖而出的高中生经常参加一系列的课外活动，希望增加他们被精选本科院校录取的机会。

paragraphs.sourceText: However, college admissions experts say that the quality of a college hopeful’s extracurricular activities matters more than the number of activities he or she participates in.
paragraphs.translationZh: 然而，大学招生专家表示，大学申请者的课外活动质量比他或她参加的活动数量更重要。

paragraphs.sourceText: Sue Rexford, the director of college guidance at the Charles E. Smith Jewish Day School, says it is not necessary for a student filling out the Common Application to list 10 activities in the application.
paragraphs.translationZh: 查尔斯·E·史密斯犹太走读学校 (Charles E. Smith Jesus Day School) 的大学指导主任苏·雷克斯福德 (Sue Rexford) 表示，学生在填写通用申请表时没有必要在申请表中列出 10 项活动。

paragraphs.sourceText: “No college will expect that a student has a huge laundry list of extracurriculars that they have been passionately involved in each for an extended period of time,” Rexford wrote in an email.
paragraphs.translationZh: 雷克斯福德在一封电子邮件中写道：“没有哪所大学会期望学生拥有一份庞大的课外活动清单，而他们在很长一段时间内都热情地参与其中。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Experts say it is tougher to distinguish oneself in a school-affiliated extracurricular activity that is common among high school students than it is to stand out while doing an uncommon activity.
paragraphs.translationZh: 专家表示，在高中生中常见的学校附属课外活动中脱颖而出，比在一项不常见的活动中脱颖而出更难。

paragraphs.sourceText: “The competition to stand out and make an impact is going to be much stiffer, and so if they’re going to do a popular activity, I’d say, be the best at it,” says Sara Harberson, a college admissions consultant.
paragraphs.translationZh: 大学招生顾问萨拉·哈伯森 (Sara Harberson) 表示：“要想脱颖而出并产生影响，竞争将会更加激烈，因此，如果他们要做一项受欢迎的活动，我想说，就要做最好的。”

paragraphs.sourceText: High school students who have an impressive personal project they are working on independently often impress colleges, experts say.
paragraphs.translationZh: 专家表示，高中生独立完成的个人项目令人印象深刻，通常会给大学留下深刻的印象。

paragraphs.sourceText: “For example, a student with an interest in entrepreneurship could demonstrate skill and potential by starting a profitable small business,” Olivia Valdes, the founder of Zen Admissions consulting firm, wrote in an email.
paragraphs.translationZh: “例如，对创业感兴趣的学生可以通过创办一家盈利的小企业来展示技能和潜力，”禅宗招生咨询公司的创始人奥利维亚·瓦尔德斯在一封电子邮件中写道。

paragraphs.sourceText: Joseph Adegboyega-Edun, a Maryland high school guidance counselor, says unconventional extracurricular activities can help students impress college admissions offices, assuming they demonstrated serious commitment. “Again, since one of the big questions high school seniors must consider is ‘What makes you unique?,’ having an uncommon extracurricular activity vs. a conventional one is an advantage,” he wrote in an email.
paragraphs.translationZh: 马里兰州高中辅导员约瑟夫·阿德博耶加-埃顿 (Joseph Adegboyega-Edun) 表示，非常规的课外活动可以帮助学生给大学招生办公室留下深刻印象，前提是他们表现出认真的承诺。他在一封电子邮件中写道：“再说一次，由于高中生必须考虑的一个大问题是‘什么让你与众不同？’，与传统的课外活动相比，进行不寻常的课外活动是一种优势。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Experts say demonstrating talent in at least one extracurricular activity can help in the college admissions process, especially at top-tier undergraduate institutions.
paragraphs.translationZh: 专家表示，在至少一项课外活动中展示才能有助于大学录取过程，尤其是在顶级本科院校。

paragraphs.sourceText: “Distinguishing yourself in one focused type of extracurricular activity can be a positive in the admissions process, especially for highly selective institutions, where having top grades and test scores is not enough,” Katie Kelley, admissions counselor at IvyWise admissions consultancy, wrote in an email. “Students need to have that quality or hook that will appeal to admissions officers and allow them to visualize how the student might come and enrich their campus community.”
paragraphs.translationZh: IvyWise 招生咨询公司的招生顾问凯蒂·凯利 (Katie Kelley) 在一封电子邮件中写道：“在一种专注的课外活动中脱颖而出，可能会对招生过程产生积极影响，特别是对于那些挑剔的院校来说，仅仅拥有最高的成绩和考试成绩是不够的。” “学生需要具备能够吸引招生人员的品质或吸引力，让他们能够想象出学生将如何来丰富他们的校园社区。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Extracurricular activities related to the college major declared on a college application are beneficial, experts suggest. “If you already know your major, having an extracurricular that fits into that major can be a big plus,” says Mayghin Levine, the manager of educational opportunities with The Cabbage Patch Settlement House, a Louisville, Kentucky, nonprofit community center.
paragraphs.translationZh: 专家建议，与大学申请中申报的大学专业相关的课外活动是有益的。 “如果你已经了解自己的专业，那么拥有适合该专业的课外活动可能会是一大优势，”肯塔基州路易斯维尔非营利性社区中心卷心菜补丁安置所 (The Cabbage Patch Settlement House) 的教育机会经理梅金·莱文 (Mayghin Levine) 说道。

paragraphs.sourceText: High school students who have had a strong positive influence on their community through an extracurricular activity may impress a college and win a scholarship, says Erica Gwyn, a former math and science magnet program assistant at a public high school who is now executive director of the Kaleidoscope Careers Academy in Atlanta, a nonprofit organization.
paragraphs.translationZh: 埃丽卡·格温 (Erica Gwyn) 表示，通过课外活动对社区产生强烈积极影响的高中生可能会给大学留下深刻的印象并赢得奖学金。埃里卡·格温曾是一所公立高中的数学和科学磁铁项目助理，现在是亚特兰大非营利组织万花筒职业学院的执行董事。

paragraphs.sourceText: With the smell of coffee and fresh bread floating in the air, stalls bursting with colourful vegetables and tempting cheeses, and the buzz of friendly chats, farmers’ markets are a feast for the senses. They also provide an opportunity to talk to the people responsible for growing or raising your food, support your local economy and pick up fresh seasonal produce — all at the same time.
paragraphs.translationZh: 空气中弥漫着咖啡和新鲜面包的香味，摊位上摆满了色彩缤纷的蔬菜和诱人的奶酪，还有友好的交谈声，农贸市场是一场感官盛宴。他们还提供了与负责种植或种植食物的人交谈、支持当地经济并购买新鲜时令农产品的机会——所有这一切都在同一时间进行。

paragraphs.sourceText: Farmers’ markets are usually weekly or monthly events, most often with outdoor stalls, which allow farmers or producers to sell their food directly to customers. The size or regularity of markets can vary from season to season, depending on the area’s agricultural calendar, and you’re likely to find different produce on sale at different times of the year. By cutting out the middleman, the farmers secure more profit for their produce. Shoppers also benefit from seeing exactly where — and to who — their money is going.
paragraphs.translationZh: 农贸市场通常每周或每月举办一次活动，最常见的是户外摊位，农民或生产者可以将他们的食物直接出售给顾客。市场的规模或规律性可能因季节而异，具体取决于该地区的农业日历，并且您可能会发现一年中不同时间出售不同的农产品。通过消除中间商，农民可以从他们的产品中获得更多利润。购物者还可以通过准确了解自己的钱流向何处以及流向谁而受益。

options.sourceText: Students whose extracurricular activity has benefited their community are likely to win a scholarship.
options.translationZh: 课外活动使社区受益的学生很可能获得奖学金。

options.sourceText: Undertaking too many extracurricular activities will hardly be seen as a plus by colleges.
options.translationZh: 进行太多的课外活动很难被大学视为一种优势。

options.sourceText: A student who exhibits abilities in doing business can impress colleges.
options.translationZh: 表现出经商能力的学生会给大学留下深刻的印象。

options.sourceText: High school students participating in a popular activity should excel in it.
options.translationZh: 参加一项受欢迎的活动的高中生应该表现出色。

options.sourceText: Engaging in uncommon activities can demonstrate students’ determination and dedication.
options.translationZh: 参与不寻常的活动可以展示学生的决心和奉献精神。

options.sourceText: It is advisable for students to choose an extracurricular activity that is related to their future study at college.
options.translationZh: 建议学生选择与未来大学学习相关的课外活动。
